about: Settings of the library-motion tool (tools/anim/README.md). The frames are drawn 1:1 at the 64 px tile: today's 16 px tile shown at 4x, the scale the cut-out demo draws at. The paces are read from content/core/params.json by these keys. The limits are what `pnpm anim check` fails on.

forager.about: The forager, the man (character-forager-m.glb), as the 3D game uses him (Mixamo bone names), lit and snapped to his ramps.
forager.credit: Forager, generated with Meshy (meshy.ai), CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (game/public3d/models/README.md); modified: posed with library motion and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

forager-f.about: The forager, the woman: long braids, neckerchief, rope belt. Mixamo bone names, the forager's scale and camera.

mage.about: The mage of the character experiments: a long dark robe. Mixamo bone names, the forager's scale and camera. Its skeleton was transferred from the warrior, not fitted to its body (the mesh is not standing on the ground plane): trial 3 found the robe torn and the props hidden; fit it as the six people were (game/tools/blender/person_rig.py) before its sheets are used.
mage.credit: Mage, generated with Meshy (meshy.ai), CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; modified: reduced from 322,614 to 59,988 triangles; skeleton and skin weights added in Blender by transferring the warrior's Mixamo-named rig (game/tools/blender/rig_transfer.py); clips Idle, Walk and Run shared from the warrior; posed with library motion and rendered to pixels by tools/anim (game/public3d/models/README.md)

rig.about: A 19-bone body rig (.blend, rigid parts on bones: hips, spine, neck, head, upper_arm/forearm/hand/tool and thigh/shin/foot per side), path from ANIM_RIG_BLEND. Heights are modelled stretched by 1/cos 30 for the 30 degree camera it was drawn for; it takes the 50 degree camera like every target, and the stretch is checked again when it is rendered at 50 (its .blend is not in the repo).

wolf.about: The wolf, dark grey (character-wolf-grim.glb): a four-legged body that carries its own Idle, Walk and Run, so nothing is retargeted ('native'). The feet are the tails of the last bone of each leg. The camera is the forager's; the scale makes the wolf about 0.9 m at the ears.
wolf.credit: Wolf, generated with Meshy (meshy.ai), CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; modified: the emission input removed (it repeated the colour map) and the colour map cut from 2048 to 1024 px; scaled to 0.9 m at the ears; Meshy's walk renamed Walk; Run made from the walk and Idle made from the standing pose in Blender (game/tools/blender/quad_pass.py); posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

hare.about: The hare (animal-hare.glb): a four-legged body that carries its own Idle, Walk and Run and the hunt's held poses Alert, Graze and Lie, so nothing is retargeted ('native'). The feet are the tails of the paw bones. The camera is the forager's; the scale makes the hare about 0.35 m at the ears, sitting.
hare.credit: Rabbit by CDmir (with TinyWorlds), OpenGameArt, CC0, https://opengameart.org/content/rabbit-0; modified: the fur-shell mesh, the lights, the camera and the ground plane removed; the Blender Internal material rebuilt as a Principled BSDF on the packed colour map, warmed and lightened toward a sandy hare; scaled to 0.35 m at the ears with the scale baked into the bones, and a tip bone under each paw (the renderer reads a foot from its bone's tail); Guarding renamed Idle; Walk and Run made from Running in Blender (game/tools/blender/hare_pass.py: Walk 1.6x slower with the swings and the bob at 0.3 of the bound's around their means and the paws' lift at 0.55 of it, Run at the bound's tempo with them at 0.5 and the lift at 0.7, the planted paws kept on the ground); Alert, Graze and Lie keyed in Blender on the rig's own controls (the same script: Guarding's sit-up with the ears pricked and the head turning, its crouch with the nose on the floor, and Dying's last frame only, rolled onto its side with the legs drawn in); the other actions dropped; posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

hare-pied.about: The hare's pied body (animal-hare-pied.glb): the hare's model and actions with white patches painted on its colour map in texture space (the back, the flanks and the face from seeded noise, the belly white), so a pied coat has its pattern fixed to the body. The hare's camera, scale, feet and ramps, plus grey for the white. Drawn only as a coat's body (the hare's coats, "body": "hare-pied").
hare-pied.credit: Rabbit by CDmir (with TinyWorlds), OpenGameArt, CC0, https://opengameart.org/content/rabbit-0; modified: the same derivative as animal-hare.glb (game/tools/blender/hare_pass.py), with white patches painted on its colour map from seeded noise (the back, the flanks and the face, the belly white) for a pied coat; posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim

crow.about: The crow (animal-crow.glb): a two-legged body that carries its own Idle, Hop and Lift, the hunt's held poses Alert, Peck and Lie (and the file's Fly), so nothing is retargeted ('native'). A bird has two feet, so the four contacts name its two toe bones twice. The camera is the forager's; the scale makes the crow about 0.3 m standing.
crow.credit: Raven by Teh_Bucket, OpenGameArt, CC0, https://opengameart.org/content/raven-0; modified: the mirror and edge-split modifiers applied (one whole mesh); the Blender Internal material rebuilt as a Principled BSDF on the packed colour map, lightened; turned to face -Y and scaled to 0.3 m standing, both baked into the bones, and a tip bone under each foot (the renderer reads a foot from its bone's tail); the tail held up so the bird stands on its feet; Idle, Hop, Lift, Alert, Peck and Lie made in Blender from the file's standing pose and its flight (game/tools/blender/crow_pass.py), the flight kept as Fly; posed with its own actions and rendered to pixels by tools/anim
